summary: Frontend UI end-to-end test of Legacy report import wizard (Engineer app) covering: customer pick -> CSV upload + AI extraction -> Review (photos, comments, two signature pads) -> Save -> Done -> PDF download. All UI mechanics work. AI extracts 3 machines from sample CSV in ~3s. Photo add/preview/remove + 3-max cap, comments textarea, both signature canvases (mouse-drag), engineer name pre-fill (Engineer Smoke), today's date defaults (2026-06-03), Clear button, Save POST 200, PDF GET 200 application/pdf all verified. ONE FUNCTIONAL CONCERN: PDF size remains ~12KB when 1 photo was uploaded — payload correctly includes file_id+storage_path+url so embedding gap is on the backend/PDF builder side, not the UI.

integration_issues.issue: Generated PDF byte-size stays ~11-13KB even after uploading 1+ photos via the Review step. The frontend correctly POSTs photos (verified payload: visit[0].machine[0].photos = [{file_id, storage_path, url}]) and the /api/files/upload call returns 200 with valid id+storage_path. Backend either (a) isn't persisting the photos array against machines, or (b) the PDF builder isn't fetching/embedding them from storage_path. Per task spec a non-trivial PDF (>~20KB) is required to confirm image embedding.

issues: Cookie consent banner overlaps the 'Next: Upload' primary action button at 1440x900 viewport, forcing users to scroll or dismiss it. Worth raising banner z-index awareness or repositioning.

action_items: Investigate why uploaded photos are not embedded in the generated PDF when the flow runs through the browser UI. Frontend payload is correct (photos:[{file_id, storage_path, url}]). Inspect POST /api/svc/legacy/reports handler to confirm it stores per-machine photos and that /pdf endpoint passes them to legacy_report_pdf.py for embedding (or that storage_path read is succeeding).

Reproduce locally: save a report with photos via UI, then call GET /api/svc/legacy/reports/{id} to see if photos persist; and call GET /pdf to compare byte-size with the direct-API smoke from iter 220i.
critical_code_review_comments: EngineerLegacyImport.js save payload (line ~276-279) filters photos by p.storage_path which is fine; matches what backend received in capture.
PDF download is via blob fetch (downloadPdf), so the legacy-done-view-pdf button is a <button> not an <a>; tests must use page.expect_response to capture the GET. Working as intended.

Machine accordions are collapsed on entry to Review even though spec notes 'machines auto-expand'. Photo block (legacy-photos-{id}) is only mounted while expanded. Consider auto-expanding the first machine (or all) on Review entry to make photos discoverable without an extra click.
Customer signature name input is not pre-filled (engineer is pre-filled with 'Engineer Smoke'). Acceptable per spec since it's customer acceptance, but signal to user could be clearer (placeholder).

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all UI flows pass; PDF photo-embedding outcome failed)

seed_data_creation: Saved 2 legacy reports for customer 'E2E Test Gym' during this session (ids 5ba89ef2-... and 89f98543-... and one more). Photos uploaded via /api/files/upload as 'service-photos' category.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login OK, navigate to /svc/engineer/legacy-import. Cookie banner overlaps the Next button — dismiss it via 'Accept All' first. Machine cards in Review are COLLAPSED by default; you must click [data-testid=legacy-machine-toggle-{id}] to render [data-testid=legacy-photos-{id}] (and thus the photo add button). AI extraction returned 3 machines from the sample CSV in ~3s. Signature canvases respond to multi-point page.mouse.move/down/up. Save POST returns {report:{id,...}} and PDF download is via blob (no href on the button — capture via page.expect_response on /legacy/reports/.../pdf).
rca of the issue: Frontend behaviour confirmed correct via payload capture: POST /api/svc/legacy/reports body contains visits[0].machines[0].photos = [{file_id, storage_path, url}], comments string, and both signatures with non-empty data_url (~9.2KB base64 each). Despite this, the subsequent GET /api/svc/legacy/reports/{id}/pdf returns 11-13KB regardless of whether 0 or 1 photo was attached. Therefore: (1) photos may not be persisted by backend, or (2) PDF builder cannot resolve storage_path → image bytes (e.g., wrong bucket / signed-url failure). Recommend asserting `len(report.visits[0].machines[0].photos) > 0` server-side after save and adding a log in legacy_report_pdf.py for each photo embed attempt.
